subject: general
question: Rabindranath Tagore referred to __________ as Nritya Samragini, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitara Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rabindranath Tagore referred to Sitara Devi as **Nritya Samragini**, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
 
• Sitara Devi was a renowned Indian dancer of the **classical Kathak style**.
 
• She was known for her **energetic style and innovative choreography** in Kathak.
 
• Sitara Devi was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** and the **Padma Shri** for her contributions to Indian dance.
 
• Her performances were acclaimed both **nationally and internationally**, inspiring many generations of dancers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It originated from the traveling bards of North India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• The dance form emphasizes intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Kathak has a strong connection with the **Bhakti Movement** and the **Mughal courts**, where it evolved as a court entertainment.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• This is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
 
• The award is given by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama**.
 
• It was established in 1952 and recognizes outstanding achievement in the performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri**
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in India.
 
• It is awarded for distinguished service in various fields including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• The award was instituted in 1954 and is announced annually on Republic Day.
 
 
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore**
 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali polymath who reshaped Bengali literature and music, as well as Indian art, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• He became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
 
• Tagore's poetry, short stories, and novels are widely celebrated and translated into many languages worldwide.
